analysis:
Compared the complete Capacity base/head source, Lifecycle metadata, patch and base source against the indexed threat model and supplied T-041 detail. Capacity.swift:82 adds an awaited selected-model recovery check to the periodic actor tick, after inventory registration and before daemon-state writing. Existing memory accounting, admission-drain masking, scoped prefix-cache evidence and heartbeat throttling are unchanged. The recovery implementation is not supplied; integration must examine its bounded execution, lifecycle/add-on hold admission gates, model identity and memory-reservation behavior (A-018, TB-007, TB-012, T-059), including whether it can delay subsequent capacity/liveness ticks.
Lifecycle.swift head patch:107–117 adds up to ten seconds of reconnect polling and treats an unacknowledged disconnected session as eligible for graceful drain success at 127–128. Visible surrounding logic still requires no remaining coordinator/local work, native-owner retirement and App Attest worker retirement; coordinatorAcknowledged remains false rather than misreporting acknowledgement. No concrete regression is established locally. However, the new success path relies on the comment's unverified contract that disconnect cancels accepted work and buffers no outbound messages. Integration must inspect hasRegisteredConnection, acknowledgeDrain and disconnect/reconnect handling to establish ordering with terminal/usage delivery, accepted-work retirement and connection-bound authorization invalidation (A-009, A-016, T-010, T-053). A snapshot of disconnected state must not conceal pending accounting or allow reconnect to reopen lifecycle-owned admission. These missing implementations are coverage limits, not evidence of missing controls. No changes to encryption, credentials, release qualification or cache cryptography are visible in these units.
